thread:
maya: Heads-up — during veridian-lite-v2 bring-up I found a weird token reorder when input mixes CJK and RTL segments. quick repro below.
liam: example?
maya: input: `日本語 متن عربي (en)`, expected detok keeps relative order, model output swaps the Arabic phrase before the Japanese punctuation.
liam: ugh. is this only on quantized builds?
maya: tried fp16 and int8 both repro but much worse on int4. numbers: fp16 BLEU 28.9, int8 BLEU 28.4, int4 BLEU 25.6 (on our small mixedscript testset).
eval-bot: automated eval summary for veridian-lite-v2 (mixedscript-reorder suite): avg BLEU delta -3.3 vs baseline, COMET -0.9, token-shift rate 1.2%. Full artifact: https://run.internal/evals/1759123456
satoshi: my first guess is tokenizer/detokenizer normalization + bidi handling. mixed CJK+RTL often trips the BPE merges when ZWJ/ZWNJ or bidi markers are present.
aisha: did you test NFC vs NFKC normalizations? sometimes kana-kanji combos change byte boundaries after normalization.
maya: yes — NFC vs NFKC changed a few merges but reorder still occurs. I also noticed bracket orientation flips for Arabic segments when followed by fullwidth punctuation.
liam: can you paste the exact eval command you ran?
maya: ```
python eval.py 
  --model veridian-lite-v2 
  --tokenizer veridian-vocab-14k.json 
  --quant q4_0 
  --suite mixedscript-reorder 
```
aisha: try running with `--preserve-bidi=true` in the detok layer (if available) and compare. also check we don't accidentally run a LTR-only postprocess.
maya: good call. trying now.
eval-bot: quick canary run (preserve-bidi=true) finished: BLEU 27.8 (int4), token-shift rate 0.6%. saving logs to https://run.internal/evals/1759123456/canary
satoshi: that’s interesting — preserving bidi halves the token-shift but BLEU still lower than int8. suggests quant kernels change sampling/softmax marginally and interact with token boundaries.
liam: could be kernel fallback ordering on some GPUs causing slight token-prob perturbations. check if int4 used fused-softmax vs reference-softmax.
maya: verified kernel table: int4 path used `softmax_v2_fallback` on some nodes. adding an experiment to force `softmax_v1_fused` to compare.
aisha: also re-run with a deterministic sampling seed and `--topk=1` to isolate greedy decode differences.
maya: running deterministic tests now. initial greedy diffs show token positions still moved in ~0.9% of cases on int4 even with same seed.
satoshi: seems like a tokenizer-level issue amplified by quant noise. action items: 1) maya: capture a minimal failing corpus & exact detok trace, 2) liam: confirm kernel selection mapping for int4 nodes, 3) aisha: try detok preserve-bidi default and NFKC pre-normalize in pipeline, 4) me (satoshi): instrument BPE merge ops to log when ZWJ/ZWNJ present.
maya: added corpus to /mnt/eval_artifacts/mixedscript-reorder/1759123456/minimal_fails.jsonl and posted a few examples in the issue tracker.
liam: thanks — I'll try forcing fused-softmax on staging and report back.
aisha: if we can get BLEU within 1.0 of fp16 by combining bidi-preserve + kernel fix, we can move ahead with int4 onboard but gate for regions with heavy RTL+CJK mixes.
maya: sounds good. filing a short ADR for onboard decision tree. :thumbsup:
liam: ping me when fused-softmax result is up.
eval-bot: test matrix queued: int4/int8/fp16 x normalize(NFC/NFKC) x preserve-bidi(true/false). ETA ~3h.
maya: thanks — I'll keep monitoring and will open a follow-up thread if we see different failure modes.
